slides.title: Why Are **You** Here Today?
slides.lead: A legal hackathon gives you a unique opportunity for
points: **Learning by doing:** law is usually taught through books and cases. Here you apply what you know to real challenges, experiment, fail, iterate and build something tangible.
**Breaking down disciplinary silos:** law students work with computer scientists, designers and entrepreneurs, learn each other's language and solve problems together.
**Shaping the future of legal services:** AI is changing the legal profession. Help shape that change, so that legal services become more accessible, efficient and human-centred.

slides.title: Some **Ground Rules**
points: **Work wherever you like**: in rooms ==61-070== and ==61-152==. **Leave the rooms as you found them.**
**Take a break** or go home to rest whenever you need to. You can also **stay here** as long as you need.
Be **cooperative**, **ask questions** and **ask the mentors** for help

slides.title: Photos and **Filming**
points: A film crew and photographers are here, for **social media** and for the **University**
If you do not want to be filmed, let us know and wear an **orange sticker**. We will then not film you, or cut you out.

slides.title: We Are Here to **Have Fun**
points: We provide food and drinks to keep you fuelled up, mate tea included 🧉
Some games later in the evening

slides.title: The **Schedule**
rows: The challenge owners present their challenges
Ask the challenge owners your questions
Hacking starts: find a workstation for your team, brainstorm and iterate
Code freeze: upload your project on the [hackathon website](https://www.legalhackathons.org/) and prepare your pitch
Pitches to the jury panels, 3 minutes per team; the rooms are announced later
slides.after: We make all announcements on Discord: join at [discord.gg/7n4pPU8tX](https://discord.gg/7n4pPU8tX)

slides.title: Choosing a **Challenge**
points: The challenge owners present their challenges next
